name: The Last Bolt of White Silk
summary: The white silk of the Concord was lost twice: the thread-quarter burned in the Sundering's autumn, and again in the Toll War's Silk Fire (~597 AA). Legend insists a single bolt survived the first fire and was hidden before the second — woven, not spun, its threads 'the river taught'. Every weaver's guild in the Crownlands claims a grandmother who touched it; no loom since has produced anything like it. If it exists, it is the last working of Concord craft that requires no caster.
origin: Concord of Weavers — Velkash's thread-quarter at its height (~150 CoW onward)
current_whereabouts: Unknown. Claimed: a Wealdmark archive, a Mile vault, a Greenwood grove-shrine, and the bottom of the Weavers' River. All four claims are mutually exclusive and equally sincere.
properties: Said to hold dye like memory holds faces — colors appear on it that were true once
Cannot be cut by shears; folds only along lines it agrees to
A hand's-breadth would fund an expedition; a full bolt could buy a realm's debt
keepers: None confirmed. The Velkash weavers' guilds maintain a joint reward for verified sighting — unclaimed for 215 years.
value_or_danger: Beyond price as relic; dangerous as symbol — whoever displays it claims the Concord's mantle.
adventure_hooks: All four claimants' evidence checks out. Players must find which tradition is copying which.
A bolt surfaces in a Mile auction with provenance papers from three different centuries.
The Thread district's oldest loom, retired and sacred, weaves three inches of white overnight. Nobody touched it.
